$comment: Provenance manifest. Nothing enters this bundle without an entry. Run the upstream-sync skill monthly.

mcp.name: next-devtools
mcp.note: Next 16+ also ships version-accurate docs at node_modules/next/dist/docs/

mcp.name: convex

mcp.name: playwright-test
mcp.note: Written by `npx playwright init-agents --loop=claude` alongside the planner/generator/healer agents in .claude/agents. That command OVERWRITES .mcp.json — after running it, restore the server list and `pnpm sync:mcp`; the health lockfile-match check catches the damage.

mcp.name: 21st
mcp.note: Magic MCP (@21st-dev/magic) was replaced by the unified 21st MCP; old keys were reset. OFF by default because the bundle's promise is fewer subscriptions. Fallback: browse 21st.dev and paste the component prompt.

scripts.$comment: Cross-platform mechanism. Node is the only runtime the bundle assumes, so every operation is a Node script behind a pnpm name and runs identically on macOS, Linux and Windows. Rationale and the full substitution table: .agents/skills/setup-health/references/platform-notes.md

entries.name: pnpm health
entries.replaces: grep -r, readlink, and the shell half of setup-health

entries.name: pnpm link:skills
entries.note: Windows: creates a directory JUNCTION (no admin needed) and repairs the plain-text stub that git writes when core.symlinks=false. Last-resort fallback is a copy plus a .claude/.skills-is-a-copy marker, reported as WARN every run.

entries.name: pnpm verify
entries.note: The definition of done: health + lint + build. Enforced in Claude Code by a Stop hook (`--hook` exits 2 to block a completion with a red build, and honors stop_hook_active so it can never trap the user). Other tools get the AGENTS.md rule plus CI.

scripts.postinstall: link-skills --soft && sync-mcp --soft — repairs both mirrors on pnpm install, never aborts the install

installer.design: Zero dependencies, in its own repo. npx installs a package before running it, so any dependency is time the user spends waiting — and npm cannot install from a subdirectory of this repo, which rules out shipping the CLI here. It downloads the GitHub tarball and unpacks it with node:zlib plus a ~40-line tar reader: no git, no curl, no tar binary, no shell, so it behaves the same on Windows.
installer.notes: The .claude/skills symlink is skipped by the tarball (symlink entries are not extracted) and recreated by postinstall's link-skills — the same repair path that fixes Windows checkouts. Publishing to npm would shorten the command to `npx create-shipkit`; that needs the owner's npm account.

mirrors.rule: Never edited directly. Byte-identical on purpose so drift detection is a string compare on every platform. Regenerate with `pnpm sync:mcp`; `pnpm check:mcp` and setup-health fail on drift.

Committed as a git symlink (mode 120000) so macOS and Linux clones work with zero steps. Windows clones without symlink support get a text stub instead; `pnpm link:skills` detects and repairs it, and postinstall runs it automatically.
Update the TOML snippet whenever .mcp.json changes.

plugins.name: nextjs
plugins.note: Official Next.js skills from the framework repo itself: Cache Components adoption, Partial Prefetching, runtime verification against a running dev server.

plugins.name: convex
plugins.note: Official skills are NOT vendored into .agents/skills — they arrive through the plugin and update themselves. That is upstream-sync by delegation. Our convex-structure skill covers only what the official ones cannot know: this repo's conventions.

plugins.name: stripe
bundles: stripe-best-practices skill (API selection, security, restricted keys, webhooks)
stripe-docs / stripe-projects / stripe-directory / upgrade-stripe / connect-recommend skills
remote MCP https://mcp.stripe.com (OAuth — no key stored anywhere)
plugins.crossTool: stripe/ai ships the SAME skills as providers for codex, cursor, grok, kiro — the cross-tool requirement is solved upstream by Stripe.
plugins.note: While on an unclaimed `stripe sandbox create` environment, use the CLI, not the MCP (Stripe's own guidance).

plugins.name: posthog
plugins.note: The MCP reads product data BACK — insights, funnels, flags, experiments, replays. That is why PostHog was chosen over Amplitude (also official) and over Plausible/Umami/Mixpanel (no official plugin at all).

plugins.name: render
plugins.alternative: railwayapp/railway-skills is equally official (one use-railway skill, mcp.railway.com, cross-tool providers). Render was chosen because render.yaml declares the WHOLE topology as committed, diffable code, while Railway services are created interactively — state the repo cannot see. Swapping is writing one file.

plugins.name: shadcn / magicui / tailwind / zustand plugins
plugins.note: Their official integration is the MCP layer in .mcp.json plus Context7 docs. Do not bundle unofficial plugins for these.

backend.$comment: Phases 2+3. Backend SOURCE ships in full: schema, waitlist, Better Auth wiring (convex/auth.ts, auth.config.ts, convex.config.ts, http.ts, the /api/auth proxy) and the Stripe billing seam (convex/billing.ts). convex/_generated/ does NOT and cannot ship: only `npx convex dev` produces it, and that opens a browser, so it is the buyer's manual step. `npx convex codegen` needs CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT too — verified 2026-08-04, not assumed.
backend.status: implemented; awaiting the buyer's `npx convex dev` + Stripe keys

stripe.apiVersionNote: Stripe's current is 2026-07-29.dahlia; the component documents 2026-04-22.dahlia and we pin what the component pins. upstream-sync flags the drift — API versions change webhook payload shapes, never blind-bump.

decisions.mode: subscription (exercises renewal/cancel/expiry; one-time is a subset)
decisions.checkout: Stripe-hosted page only — card data never touches this origin (SAQ A). Embedded Payment Element requires a deliberate CSP review first.
decisions.sandboxFirst: stripe sandbox create works with no Stripe account; live mode is a later deliberate step.
decisions.plans: browser sends a plan KEY ("pro"), never a price ID or amount; price IDs live in Convex env as STRIPE_PRICE_* set at onboarding

stripe.secrets: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (prefer rk_), STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET — Convex env only; pnpm health CRITICALs on either in .env.local and on any sk_live/rk_live there

email.seam: convex/email.ts — the only file importing the Resend SDK
email.safetyDefault: testMode: true. Resend then accepts ONLY its own test inboxes, so a wrong address in development cannot reach a real person. It flips to false together with requireEmailVerification: true in convex/auth.ts, after a sending domain is verified — pnpm health fails CRITICAL on the mismatch in either direction.
email.secrets: RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, EMAIL_FROM — Convex env only
email.note: The component bundles workpool + rate-limiter, so sends are enqueued inside the calling transaction and retried by the component. No hand-rolled retry logic.

analytics.seam: src/lib/analytics.ts — typed AnalyticsEvent union; components never import posthog-js
analytics.cspDecision: Traffic is proxied through /ingest on our own origin via next.config.ts rewrites, so connect-src stays 'self' — no analytics origin is ever added to the CSP, and ad blockers do not silently drop technical users' data. PostHog's own recommended setup. Requires skipTrailingSlashRedirect: true.
analytics.privacyDefaults: person_profiles: identified_only · autocapture: false · maskAllInputs in replay · maskTextSelector [data-private] · no key means init never runs
analytics.keys: phc_ project key is public → .env.local. phx_ personal key is a full-access credential and is CRITICAL if found (matched as prefix+payload, so docs naming phx_ do not false-positive).

rejected.amplitude: official plugin exists, but events-first — weaker read-back loop
rejected.plausible / umami / mixpanel: no official plugin in claude-plugins-official as of 2026-08-04

deploy.buildCommand: corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && npx convex deploy --cmd 'pnpm build'
deploy.buildReason: convex deploy pushes the backend to the PROD deployment and only then builds the frontend with the prod URL injected. `pnpm build` alone ships a frontend against a stale backend — the most common Convex production failure.
deploy.secretSplit: Render holds CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY + public keys only. Every backend secret lives in the prod Convex deployment's env, which is what keeps live Stripe keys off dev machines (rule R7).

rejected.railway: equally official, but services are created interactively — topology the repo cannot see. Swapping to it is writing one file.

deploy.deferred: domain (Cloudflare or Namecheap). HSTS ships with a two-year max-age, so the certificate must be right on the first request at a custom domain.

preLoginContract.mechanism: src/lib/convex-api.ts exports anyApi (public export of convex/server) until convex/_generated/api exists; tsconfig excludes convex/ so the Next build never typechecks imports of a directory that is not there yet.
preLoginContract.afterLogin: one line in src/lib/convex-api.ts switches to the generated api, enabling end-to-end types
preLoginContract.onboarding: pnpm onboard prints the sequence and the single next command; pnpm health reports every unconnected piece as WARN, never FAIL
preLoginContract.rule: Never fabricate or stub convex/_generated/. A stub typechecks and then lies about the shape of every function.

referenceDomain.reason: The waitlist was shipped as working code until 2026-08-04, then moved into the skill as a worked example. A scaffold must not contain anything the buyer has to delete before starting — demo code is boilerplate, and half of it survives into production. The example still teaches every rule (indexed dedupe, O(1) counter instead of a scan, public vs internal, capped input, the blocks/features split); it just teaches instead of shipping.
referenceDomain.shippedSchema: one `counters` table, so `npx convex dev` has something valid to deploy on the first run. Delete it once a real table exists.

distribution.$comment: The repo doubles as a plugin marketplace. All manifests point at .agents/skills/ — one copy of every skill regardless of delivery path. Validate the Claude side with `claude plugin validate .` (strict passes as of 2026-08-06; a local end-to-end marketplace-add + install was also performed and then removed).

codex.verified: manifest shape mirrored from working plugins (caveman, convex, vercel); no Codex CLI on this machine to end-to-end test

auth.pinReason: PROVEN 2026-08-04, not theoretical: better-auth 1.6.25 sits INSIDE the adapter's declared peer range (>=1.6.11 <1.7.0) and still breaks the adapter's types (AuthClient useSession data resolves to never; build fails). 1.6.15 is what the adapter repo itself develops against. Exact pin — even a tilde re-admits the breakage. upstream-sync may move the pin only after building against the candidate version.
risks: Better Auth joined Vercel (Jul 2026); Convex is a competitor. Integration remains actively promoted by Convex as of Aug 2026, and both projects are open source. The auth seam keeps a swap to Clerk or Convex Auth an afternoon's work.
A DoS advisory was reported against @convex-dev/better-auth. pnpm audit runs in setup-health.

alternatives.convex-auth: lighter, fewer features, no orgs/2FA — Convex's own team has signalled a rework
alternatives.clerk: when you want someone else on-call for auth: orgs, MFA, admin UI, compliance. Costs a subscription and caps AI automation at ~70% because its dashboard steps cannot be scripted.

pins.$comment: The machine-checked set — scripts/health.mjs compares every entry against package.json. 'N.x' pins the major; a full 'x.y.z' means EXACT, range forms are a FAIL. better-auth's exact pin is load-bearing: 1.6.25 sits inside ^1.6.15 and still breaks the adapter's types (heal-ledger.md 2026-08-04). The narrative for backend pins lives in backend.auth.pins; this block is what the script enforces.

assets.$comment: Files vendored INTO the repo rather than fetched at build time. Committed on purpose: next/font/google downloads the face during `next build`, so a host with no egress cannot build at all — that took out CI here once (.agents/heal-ledger.md, 2026-08-05). Only redistributable licences may appear here; scripts/fetch-font.mjs enforces the split and keeps non-redistributable Fontshare faces gitignored.
